This only works with certain species of fish. A lot of the deep ocean fish that are overfished are unsuitable for farming for any or all of the following reasons:

1.) Their feed conversion ratio is too high. For instance, wikipedia says that bluefin tuna has a feed conversion ration of 15:1, which means it takes 15 pounds of food for the fish to gain 1 pound of marketable weight. That makes farming these fish very expensive.

2.) Some fish produce huge amounts of waste that are difficult to deal with in a farming environment.

3.) Some fish just don't do well in a farming environment in general. Farmed salmon, for example, have to be given all kinds of antibiotics just to keep them from dying. Many of these animals evolved to roam the open seas, not to live a sedentary lifestyle sitting in a small farming pond with a few thousand other fish, and getting without having it drastically affect the flavor, texture, and nutritional content of the harvested meat is tricky, to say the least, and often requires practices that most people would not enjoy hearing about. For example, farmed salmon have to be fed pigmentation or their meat will be gray instead of pink.

So "just farm everything" is a lot more difficult than you imply. The technology is getting better but it's not there yet, and until it gets there we have to do something else or be prepared to watch the fisheries collapse.
